title: HashSet Against the Quadratic
prompt:
`DuplicateFinder.HasAny(List<int>, List<int>)` scans the whole
`List` per candidate — O(n·m). Rewrite as
`Solution.HasAny(List<int> haystack, List<int> needles)` that puts the
haystack in a `System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<int>` once and tests each
needle in ~O(1):

- true iff at least one needle is present,
- empty needles → false, empty haystack → false,
- duplicates in either side are irrelevant.

```csharp
public static class Solution
{
    public static bool HasAny(System.Collections.Generic.List<int> haystack,
                              System.Collections.Generic.List<int> needles);
}
```

tests.name: membership semantics
tests.hint: Build the set once, test each needle against it.

tests.name: degenerate inputs
tests.hint: Empty side means no match can exist.

tests.name: duplicates do not matter
tests.code:
var hay = new System.Collections.Generic.List<int> { 5, 5, 5 };
Cj.True(Solution.HasAny(hay, new System.Collections.Generic.List<int> { 5, 5 }), "dup on both sides still matches");
tests.hint: A set collapses duplicates; presence is all that counts.
